title: Exploring students’ perspectives on Generative AI-assisted academic writing
extended_summary:
This paper examines how students perceive and experience generative AI (GenAI) when used to support academic writing. Rather than testing whether GenAI improves writing outcomes experimentally, the study asks what roles students expect AI to play, what benefits they perceive during writing, and what barriers they encounter while using it. The motivation is to better understand the student side of GenAI-assisted writing and to inform future educational AI and instructional design.

The intervention/context was a ChatGPT-4-embedded writing system called Writing With GPT (WWG), developed by the research team. Twenty students in higher education completed an English academic writing task with the system and then participated in semi-structured interviews. The participants were Chinese students at an English-medium international joint-venture university in Suzhou, mainland China, spanning bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels, with varying IELTS scores and AI literacy levels.

The study found that students expected GenAI to function as a multi-tasking writing assistant, a private virtual tutor, and a digital peer. They perceived benefits in ideation, planning, drafting, revision, writing quality, writing speed, topic knowledge, enjoyment, question generation, perceived support, and self-efficacy. At the same time, they identified substantial barriers, including hallucination, weak contextual and cultural understanding, limited higher-order thinking, lack of human/relationship/pedagogical awareness, interoperability issues, explainability gaps, and their own limitations in AI literacy, critical thinking, topic knowledge, and writing skill. Overall, the paper argues that GenAI can support academic writing, but its effectiveness depends on student capabilities and the system’s pedagogical and contextual fit.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI chatbot and writing assistant used for dialogue, drafting, feedback, and language support.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper studied a ChatGPT4-embedded writing system called Writing With GPT (WWG) to support students during an academic writing task; students used it for ideation, planning, drafting, revision, proofreading, and interactive support.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative mixed-methods interview study with 20 higher-education participants, not an experimental evaluation of outcomes. It provides direct evidence about student perceptions and experienced affordances/barriers, but not causal evidence of learning gains.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived advantages such as improved writing quality, speed, and self-efficacy, but it does not report quantitative effect sizes or comparative outcome data versus business-as-usual. As a result, impact on K-12 reading/literacy outcomes cannot be established from this study.
